prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2001 summary (max 500 words)

Core values and priorities
- Principles: Freedom, Justice, Honesty. Invest in people; be open about costs. A “green thread” runs through all policies.
- Immediate focuses: more funding for schools and hospitals; more police; higher basic state pension; free personal care for the elderly.

Health
- Cut waiting times via capacity: recruit 27,500 nurses, 4,600 doctors, 10,250 allied professionals; add 10,000 beds; boost low-paid NHS staff pay by ~£1,000/year.
- Prevention first: restore free dental and eye checks; expand scanning/diagnostics; £500m to restore access to NHS dentistry.
- Free personal care for long-term needs (as in Scotland).
- Less central micromanagement; patient care guarantees; tackle “postcode lottery” with a national Pharmaceutical Agency; no-fault compensation; end mixed wards; anti-age discrimination.

Education, skills and employment
- Funded by +1p on basic income tax (c. £3bn/yr).
- Schools: cut primary classes to avg 25; +5,000 secondary teachers; 40,000 classroom assistants (esp. KS1); paid prep time; more books/ICT; scrap PRP; reduce bureaucracy/testing (end SATs at 7); reform Ofsted; broader curriculum and music tuition.
- Higher education: abolish tuition fees UK-wide; restore grants for poorest; raise loan repayment threshold; improve academic pay/fairness.
- FE/lifelong learning: entitlements up to Level 2/3; simplify funding/qualifications.
- Jobs/training: SME training incentives; paid study leave (16–24s); replace New Deal with a Flexible Guarantee and a combined Benefits & Jobs Agency.

Law, order and justice
- +6,000 police; +2,000 part-time community officers; Community Safety Force for nuisance crime; independent complaints system; focus on prevention and cutting reoffending (work, skills, rehab in prisons).
- Victims’ rights to be heard; retain jury trials; end most mandatory sentences; hate crime units; youth justice focused on rehabilitation/restorative justice.

Transport
- Free off‑peak local buses for pensioners/disabled; aim half-price for under‑19s in full-time education.
- Reward cleaner cars (abolish VED for greenest); no real-terms rise in fuel duty next Parliament.
- Invest in public transport, reopen lines/stations; rural transport fund; enable local congestion/parking charges to fund improvements.
- Stronger regulation via a Sustainable Transport Authority; restructure Railtrack into a public-interest model; modernise London Underground through a not‑for‑profit bond‑funded company; tighter safety oversight. NATS kept public; restrict noisy night flights.

Pensions, wages, benefits
- Raise basic pension (£5 weekly; more for 75+ and 80+), scrap savings penalties; create an Independent Pensions Authority. Fund via 50% tax on income over £100k.
- Minimum wage: annual review; same rate for 16+.
- Child poverty: +£200/yr for families 12+ months on income support.
- Replace CSA with family courts; longer-term aim to lift lowest earners out of tax by abolishing the 10p band.

Business, consumers and environment
- Cut red tape; £1,500 small business rates allowance; strengthen competition and consumer protection; tighter bank rules; employee consultation and H&S enforcement; ban compulsory retirement ages.
- Climate: replace Climate Change Levy with carbon tax; 10% renewables by 2010 (rising annually); phase out nuclear over time; major recycling and home energy efficiency drives.

Democracy, rights and communities
- Electoral reform: AV+ referendum for Westminster; STV for local/European; replace Lords with elected Senate; stronger Parliament and FOI; votes at 16.
- Equality Act and Commission; repeal Section 28; judge‑approved surveillance; no ID cards; fairer, faster asylum with dignity.
- Devolution: more powers to nations/regions; local income tax to replace Council Tax.
- Rural/urban renewal: brownfield-first planning; one-stop regeneration funds; CAP/CFP reforms; Ministry for Rural Affairs; protect local services, seas and green spaces.

Europe, foreign policy, defence, economy
- Pro‑EU reform: constitutional settlement, transparency, enlargement; euro entry by referendum at a competitive rate.
- Foreign policy based on human rights; end subsidies for arms exports; support UN/ICC; maintain defence spend, retain minimum nuclear deterrent; oppose US NMD.
- Economy: strengthen Bank of England independence; “Green Budget”; transparent taxes (citizen tax contract); CGT reforms to fund police/transport.
